gloss: Western-style residence built for foreign residents

definitions.gloss: Western-style house from the foreign settlements; ijinkan
definitions.explanation: A Western-style residence built in the Meiji and Taisho periods for foreign merchants and diplomats living in Japan's treaty ports. Surviving ones in Kobe, Nagasaki, and Yokohama are preserved as tourist attractions.

examples.japanese: {神戸|こうべ}の{異人館|いじんかん}を{見|み}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to see the ijinkan in Kobe.

examples.japanese: この{異人館|いじんかん}は{明治時代|めいじじだい}に{建|た}てられた。
examples.english: This ijinkan was built in the Meiji period.

examples.japanese: {坂|さか}の{上|うえ}に{並|なら}ぶ{異人館|いじんかん}からは、{港|みなと}{全体|ぜんたい}が{見渡|みわた}せる。
examples.english: From the ijinkan lined up at the top of the slope, you can look out over the whole harbor.

notes:
Literally "foreigner's building," from {異人|いじん} — an older word for a foreigner — plus {館|かん} (hall, mansion). The word is tied to the treaty-port era and is not used for modern housing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {異人館|いじんかん}{街|がい}: an ijinkan district
- {神戸|こうべ}{北野|きたの}の{異人館|いじんかん}: the ijinkan of Kitano in Kobe
- {異人館|いじんかん}{巡|めぐ}り: touring the ijinkan

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {洋館|ようかん}: Western-style house — the general term, including houses built for Japanese owners
- {洋風|ようふう}{建築|けんちく}: Western-style architecture — a description of style, not a historical class of building
